skills.name: Retelling texts in a coherent sequence

note.text: Retelling reorganises a source into a clear account of its events while keeping their relationships. Distinguish the order in which events happened from the order in which a narrator revealed them. Before, after and because express different relations: succession alone does not prove cause. A retelling can compress details but should retain a turning point and not invent dialogue, motives or an outcome.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to reconstruct events while preserving order, causes and the source’s limits. Builds on: narrative features and lexical precision. Leads to: word choice and narrative composition.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original source: When the group arrived, the hall was locked. They checked their notice and called the organiser. Only after the organiser confirmed a different room did they move the chairs. Retelling: The locked hall prompted the group to check its notice and seek clarification; following confirmation, it moved to another room. The account must not say they forced entry or moved before confirmation.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: List events with time clues. Mark causes only where supported. Retell with clear references and consistent tense, then compare every action against the source. If the source leaves a result unknown, retain that limit.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: The group checks before moving to the confirmed room.
The locked hall prompts a check in the model.
Confirmation of another room changes the group’s action.
The retelling does not invent forced entry.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: After and before express the same order. Correction: Time connectors determine different event relationships.
Any earlier event must cause every later event. Correction: Time order alone does not establish causation.
A retelling should omit every consequential change. Correction: The source’s important change helps explain what follows.
Inventing dialogue is always permitted in a factual retelling. Correction: Unstated additions must not be presented as source events.

pick.q: Original source: Bih found the note after the meeting had ended. Which event came earlier?
w: Both are stated to be simultaneous
The text supplies no time relationship
e: After places the finding later.
The connector does not indicate simultaneity.
After supplies a relative order.

pick.q: Original source: Ayuk checked the address before posting the letter. Which retelling preserves order?
pick.r: He verified the address, then posted the letter
w: He posted it, then checked the address
He checked every letter in the town
e: That reverses before.
The source includes posting.
That adds an unsupported universal action.
pick.y: Keep the check before the posting.

pick.q: Original source: Rain began; later the lights failed. No cause is supplied. Which retelling respects the evidence?
pick.r: Rain began before the lights failed; the cause is not stated
w: Rain is proved to have caused the failure
The lights failed before rain began
The source proves no other cause is possible
e: Sequence alone does not prove causation.
That reverses the order.
Other explanations are not excluded.
pick.y: Preserve sequence without inventing a cause.
